core.title: Keep wagon manifests and feature files cross-referenced both ways
core.given: The plan contains feature files and/or wagon manifests with features[] entries.
core.when: The planner authors, edits, moves, deletes or reviews any of them.
core.then: Every feature file is referenced by its wagon manifest's features[], and every features[] entry resolves to an existing feature file.
prefer: Update features[] in the same change that adds, renames or removes a feature file.
Record an intentionally wagon-less feature in the orphan-feature allow-list instead of leaving it silently unreferenced.
avoid: A feature file no wagon manifest lists (feature -> wagon gap).
A features[] entry pointing to a missing, renamed or deleted feature file (wagon -> feature gap).
Recording a feature that does belong to a wagon on the orphan allow-list just to silence the coverage check.
unless: The feature is recorded in the orphan-feature allow-list (exempts only the feature -> wagon direction; features[] entries must still resolve).
core.why: Coverage means each feature is referenced by its wagon and vice versa; a one-sided link leaves untracked features or dangling references, breaking plan traceability.
evidence: The feature -> wagon coverage check passes: every feature file is referenced by its wagon manifest (excluding orphan-allow-listed features).
The wagon -> feature coverage check passes: every wagon features[] entry has a corresponding feature file.
verification: Two repository-wide coverage checks over the plan tree: direction feature -> wagon — every feature file must be referenced by its wagon manifest, with the orphan allow-list as the only exception; direction wagon -> feature — every features[] entry must resolve to an existing feature file, with no exceptions authored.
The allow-list exemption is one-directional: it never excuses a dangling features[] entry, and the wagon -> feature direction admits no exceptions.
Per-rule disposition: documentation-only — the obligation guides authors and reviewers; the checks report coverage gaps rather than block.
Out of scope: references between a wagon and its parent (train) artifacts, which belong to the parent-level coverage convention.

fires: The planner adds a new feature file without adding it to its wagon manifest's features[] list.
The planner adds a features[] entry pointing to a feature file that does not exist.
The planner renames or deletes a feature file, leaving a stale features[] entry.
The planner edits or reviews a plan where a pre-existing feature file is not referenced by its wagon manifest, even with no structural edit and no coverage check run yet.
The planner inspects a wagon manifest (including one whose wagon has no feature files) containing a dangling features[] entry, with no current structural edit or coverage finding.
A feature file exists (not allow-listed) whose wagon manifest is missing or does not list it.
A coverage check reports an unreferenced feature or a dangling wagon features[] reference.
doesNotFire: The feature file is recorded in the orphan-feature allow-list (exempts the feature -> wagon direction only).
Edits to train <-> wagon references only (covered by the parent-level, train coverage convention).
Content-only edits to a feature file when every feature file is already listed by its wagon and every features[] entry already resolves.

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete plan-artifact kinds this rule links — the wagon manifest (with its features[] list) and the feature file. The core activates on the neutral kinds wagon_manifest and feature_file; the profile maps them to the stack's concrete artifact kinds (in Bun, feature_file -> feature_yaml). Presence of either kind activates the rule and is what the coverage checks compare.
How feature files and wagon manifests are recognized as plan artifacts on disk (suffix or name pattern); the concrete serialization (YAML) is known only here, never in the core.
The plan tree the bidirectional coverage checks scan for wagon manifests and feature files.
profileRequirements.bunValue: plan tree (bun.json: 'The plan contains feature YAML files and/or wagon manifests...', 'a feature YAML file in the plan tree')

profileRequirements.meaning: The named allow-list in which intentionally wagon-less features are recorded, exempting them from the feature -> wagon direction only.

proposedKeys.meaning: Named allow-lists by which the stack records intentional exceptions for specific checks; this rule needs the orphan-feature allow-list holding features intentionally listed by no wagon.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: No existing key names artifact-level exception lists: enforcement.suppression_marker is a time-boxed per-rule suppression syntax, and roots.excluded only removes trees from scanning; neither is a named allow-list of individually exempted artifacts.

neutralityNotes: Wagon, feature, features[], train and 'the plan tree' are plan-structure vocabulary shared across stacks (cf. the layout and urn profile groups), so they remain in the core. The core's activation uses the serialization-neutral artifact-role kind feature_file; the concrete kind feature_yaml and its YAML recognition live only in profile values (roles.plan_artifact.kinds maps feature_file -> feature_yaml; suffix.plan_artifact carries the YAML suffix). The profile also supplies the plan root and the orphan allow-list name (proposed key enforcement.allowlists). Validator and finding ids (test_all_features_in_wagon_manifest, test_all_wagon_feature_refs_exist) and the term id wagon_feature_coverage are realization details and remain bunOnly. bun.json's per-fact activation notes are preserved elsewhere rather than as note fields on the core facts: 'either kind alone suffices' by core.given, 'the invariant holds continuously, not only on structural edits' by fires[3] and fires[4], and 'change/finding facts are additional triggers, not required for firing' by their needs_new_observer observability plus fires[6]. How a feature's owning wagon is determined (directory placement vs. manifest listing) is not specified by bun.json, so the core leaves it to the realization's check.
